test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 13 April 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a circle of diameter 20 cm, chords AB and CD are parallel to each other. BC is diameter. If AB is 6 cm from the centre of the circle, what is the length (in cm) of the chord CD?
solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 20 cm

AB = 6cm

**Concept used:**

Base = √(Hypotenuse2 - Perpendicular2)

The shortest distance on the cord from the centre is the perpendicular

The shortest distance divides the chord into two equal parts

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60358b78590766b089a8e7e864b2e521329879da4016d5b5c3bdde2a7f555c16.png] 

**Here, AB || CD and AB and CD chords are connected to the two points of diameter BC**

**Then, AB = CD**

OP ⊥ AB

Radius(OB) = 20/2 = 10 cm

So, PB = √(10² - 6²) = √(100 - 36) = √64 = 8 cm

Then, AB = (PB + PA) = 8 + 8 = 16 cm

∴ CD = AB = 16 cm

**∴ The length (in cm) of the chord CD is 16 cm**
